caveats: Administrations were injected through the admin debugger endpoints (/api/admin/bolus, /api/admin/infusion), which dispatch the same MedicationAdministrationEvent into EventService that HL7 RAS does; the Mayo RAS parse-and-persist leg upstream of that dispatch was not exercised.

The new PostInsulinGlucoseCheckJob cancellation in handleCaseStop (fix item 3) is unreachable on the CLOSE_APP path: OperationService.stopOperation already calls jobService.deleteAllJobs(caseId) before scheduledRuleEngine.handleCaseStop runs, so the 'Cancelled post-insulin-glucose-check ... (case stop)' log line never appeared in any run. The observable outcome (job gone at case close) holds; the added code is redundancy, not the acting mechanism.
Forcing the rule to re-fire for the item-2 checks required a direct UPDATE of public.qrtz_triggers.next_fire_time rather than waiting for the natural hourly trigger.
Only the mayo-mayo tenant was exercised; MGB/demo behaviour was not re-checked, though the ticket establishes the leak is Mayo-specific.
Docker Desktop crashed partway through the session; containers were restarted and every scenario reported here was re-run or re-confirmed afterwards against verified class checksums.

automation.assessment: Unit coverage from the two fix commits is already strong and matches what was observed at runtime: ScheduledRuleEngineTest.insulinAdministration_caseAlreadyClosed_doesNoWorkAtAll, insulinAdministration_afterProcedureEndWithNoCaseEndTime_stillSchedules, handleCaseStop_cancelsPostInsulinGlucoseCheckJobToo and handleCaseStop_oneGroupFailing_stillCancelsTheOther; PostInsulinGlucoseCheckScheduledRuleTest.testEvaluationPastCaseEndAbstainsEvenWhenAlertWouldFire, testEvaluationInsideCaseWindowAlertsEvenWithEndTimeRecorded, testEvaluationPastProcedureEndStillAlertsWithNoCaseEndTime and testCaseEndSilencesReminderWithProcedureEndAlsoRecorded; and EventServiceTimingEventDispatchTest pins that procedure finish no longer emits CANCEL_POST_INSULIN_GLUCOSE_CHECK_REMINDERS. Nothing there needs duplicating. The gap is the wiring level nothing currently covers: no test asserts that a Quartz job is or is not actually armed for a case, which is where the leak was visible in production (job_metadata rows created after operations.end_time). qa-suite has an insulin-glucose spec (INS-001 through INS-007) that already drives cases and medication administrations through the admin API, so the new cases belong there as supplemental.
proposed_tests: INS-008 (@supplemental): insulin administration posted on a case whose end_time is already set arms no post-insulin-glucose-check job - assert via the admin Quartz/job listing that no job exists for the case, with a same-shape open-case control in the same test so the absence assertion is provably able to fail.

INS-009 (@supplemental): a post-insulin-glucose-check reminder armed on an open case survives a procedure-finish event and is cancelled only by case close - assert the job is present after PROCEDURE_END and gone after CLOSE_APP.

Backend test in ScheduledRuleEngineTest: assert no post-insulin-glucose-check job_metadata row is ever created with created_date after operations.end_time, driving the closed-case path through the real EventService dispatch rather than a mocked jobService, so the guard is pinned at the wiring level and not just at the unit boundary.

jira_comment:
Validated deploy-ready against a throwaway local instance built from 5ee1adcde, tenant mayo-mayo.

Positive: an insulin bolus on an open case armed the reminder - the log showed 'post-insulin glucose check - reminder in 1 hour' and a post-insulin-glucose-check row appeared in job_metadata and qrtz_triggers. An ongoing insulin infusion on an open case fired a-insulin-glucose-check end to end. A procedure-finish event no longer cancels the reminder; the trigger survived it and was removed only on case close, which is the behaviour agreed in the comments above.

Negative: the case was closed, then a second insulin administration was posted with an intraop administration time - clinically inside the window, documented after close, the exact Mayo lag described in the ticket. The engine logged 'Case ... is already closed - skip insulin scheduling' and no job was created. Separately, once end_time was set on a case with an armed reminder, the next firing evaluated and abstained instead of alerting.

Red check: the pre-fix ScheduledRuleEngine was compiled and swapped into the running container. Bytecode of the unmodified source matched the shipped class exactly before the swap. With the guard removed, the same closed-case scenario armed a reminder whose job_metadata row was created two hours after end_time - the production signature in this ticket. The same was done for the rule's case-ended abstain, which then alerted three minutes past case end. Both classes were restored and checksum-verified, and the scenarios were re-run to confirm the fixed behaviour returned.

One note: the cancellation added to handleCaseStop never runs on the CLOSE_APP path, because stopOperation already deletes all jobs for the case beforehand. The outcome is correct either way; the added code is redundancy rather than the acting mechanism.

Unit coverage from the fix commits is already thorough. Automation to follow will add supplemental qa-suite cases INS-008 and INS-009 covering job-armed-or-not at the wiring level, which nothing currently asserts.
